removed text: — mine and tentative: "Come hither with your chariot of the three seats, the threefold, three-wheeled, well-rolling one."

— mine and tentative: "May the Aśvins' well-praised chariot, three-wheeled, honey-bearing, drawn by swift horses, come this way; three-seated, bountiful, bringing all good fortune, may it bring well-being to us, to our bipeds and quadrupeds."
— mine and tentative: "Why is *uṣas* so called? Because (she) *ucchati* (dispels); truly she is the later time of the night."
— mine and tentative: "*candra* (is) from *candati*, which has the sense of shining/being lovely."
— mine and tentative: "the acts by which (people) wish to go to heaven are *diviṣṭayaḥ*."
— mine and tentative: "bring together for us wealth desirable to all; put in us all riches."
— mine and tentative: "may your yoked bay horses, O mighty Indra, bring hither your chariot that all desire."
— mine and tentative: "may great prayer go forth to Vāyu, to the great wealth desired by all, the chariot-filler."
— mine and tentative: "whom heaven and earth have caused to grow, whom the *hotṛ* worships, desired by all."
— mine and tentative: "with the Ādityas, Aditi who is kind to all; Bṛhaspati, with the praisers, desired by all."
— mine and tentative: "O Indra and Varuṇa, place in us wealth desired by all, rich in good things, abounding in food."
— mine and tentative: "give wealth desired by all."
— mine and tentative: "this *cit* has many functions."
— mine and tentative: "I sprinkle you together with the sacrificial formula — offspring, long life and wealth."
— mine and tentative: "food, indeed, is *vāja*."
— mine and tentative: "the red cows (are) of the Uṣases [i.e. their vehicles]."
— mine and tentative: "the stars are, indeed, the houses of the gods."
— mine and tentative: "whoever sacrifices here attains that world: (this is) the starhood of the stars."
— mine and tentative: "these lights that are the stars are, indeed, those of the doers of good."
— mine and tentative: "*nakṣatrāṇi* from *nakṣati*, a verb of motion; and the Brāhmaṇa [says] 'these are the *kṣatras*'."
— mine and tentative: "*aktubhiḥ* (means) by the nights."
— mine and tentative: "one should seek health from the Sun."
— mine and tentative: "the Moon was born of the mind; the Sun was born of the eye."
— mine and tentative: "after him, as he shines, all shines; by his light all this shines."
— mine and tentative: "the Maruts are, indeed, the people (clan) of the gods."
— mine and tentative: "*svar* is the Āditya (the Sun)."
— mine and tentative: "for him Mitra and Varuṇa were born."
— mine and tentative: "Mitra and Varuṇa, Dhātṛ and Aryaman."
— mine and tentative: "the worlds are called *rajāṃsi*."
— mine and tentative: "the *haritas* (tawny ones) are the Āditya's."
— mine and tentative: "the Āditya is *śundhyu* from 'purifying'; [they are] his own."
— mine and tentative: "he says '*ud vayaṃ tamasas pari*'; darkness is, indeed, sin: he strikes sin away from him."
— mine and tentative: "heaven is, indeed, the world; the Sun is the highest light; he is established, in the end, in the world of heaven."
— mine and tentative: "he says '*aganma jyotir uttamam*'; the Āditya is, indeed, the highest light: he attains union with the Āditya himself."
— mine and tentative: "the last triad is the destroyer of disease."
— mine and tentative: "*radhyati* is in the sense of 'bringing under control'; the sense is 'leading (them) under my control'."
— mine and tentative: "by the grace of this blessed one, may I not go under the power of an enemy."
— mine and tentative: "for, becoming a ram, he carried off Medhātithi, the Kāṇvāyana."
— mine and tentative: "or, 'they shine by truth'; or, 'they exist by truth'."
— mine and tentative: "the gods who were friends abandoned (you); let your friendship, O Indra, be with the Maruts."
— mine and tentative: "for the Maruts did not abandon him."
— mine and tentative: "of her were born Indra and Vivasvān."
— mine and tentative: "strike, O lord; slay; show your valour."
— mine and tentative: "and *parvan* [a joint, a hill-ridge] (is) from *pṛ* 'to fill' or from *prī* 'to please'."
— mine and tentative: "The gods and the Asuras competed. Then the Asuras, from pride, 'we will offer to nobody', went about offering into their own mouths, and were defeated."
— mine and tentative: "the root *radh* is in the sense of 'coming under control'."
— mine and tentative: "when there is a collection of ant-hill fat, he wins the very sap (*ūrj*), the essence, of the earth."
— mine and tentative: "from whose might heaven and earth both trembled."
— mine and tentative: "having become Menā of Vṛṣaṇaśva, the bounteous one dwelt in the family [?]."
— mine and tentative: "Vṛṣaṇaśva had a daughter named Menā; Indra desired her."
— mine and tentative: "the Pajras, the Aṅgirasas, desiring cattle, practised austerity."
— mine and tentative: "*atya* [means] horse."
— mine and tentative: "Homage to the ocean, to the knowing one, to the lord of the rivers."

— mine and tentative: "He caused the waters to fall upon the ember; from that Ekata was born; he caused a second to fall — from that Dvita was born; he caused a third to fall — from that Trita was born."
— mine and tentative: "wealth is scattered in it [the battle]."
— mine and tentative: "this [root] has the sense of serving."
…in the dwelling you [pervaded…], and you slew Vṛtra and also Namuci. *(mine, tentative)*
You slew Namuci, the sacrifice-seeking [?] dāsa, making a [?] for the seer. *(mine, tentative)*
Here you cut off the head of the dāsa Namuci, wishing a way for Manu. *(mine, tentative)*
You made me your yoke-fellow, O Indra, and then crushed the head of the dāsa Namuci. *(mine, tentative)*
Like a falcon [bringing] the exhilarating soma-stalk to him, crushing the head of the dāsa Namuci. *(mine, tentative)*
— mine and tentative: "*radh* is [a root] in the sense of 'coming under control'."
— mine and tentative: "*ṛñj* is [a verb] of the action of adorning."
— mine and tentative: "the waters are indeed the life-breaths."
— mine and tentative: "*upara*, *upala*, is a cloud: in it the clouds come to rest; or [it is] the waters brought to a halt."
— mine and tentative: "*bhīma* [is he] of whom [others] are afraid."
mine and tentative: "Come, O Aśvins, with the three-seated, threefold chariot."

mine and tentative: "'She dawns' (*ucchati*), being true: *uchī* in the sense of 'to drive away'; for she drives away the darknesses; therefore, as she drives away (*ucchati*), this name '*uṣā*' is given to her. Again, who is this Uṣas? The later time of the night."
mine and tentative: "*Uṣas* from *vaṣṭi* (the root *vaś*), 'to shine, to desire'; from *ucchati* [it is] the other, the middle-region one."
mine and tentative: "*dyumna* (is from) *dyotati*, 'it shines': fame, or food."
mine and tentative: "you, O Jātavedas, desired by all, in the house [we seat?] our prayers"
mine and tentative: "*dyumna* (is from) *dyotate*, 'it shines': fame or food."
mine and tentative: "from *ṛ*, 'to go', a verb of motion."
mine and tentative: "*sūrya* (is) from *sṛ*, 'to go'; or from *su*, 'to impel'; or from *svīryate*."
mine and tentative: "The rays, the *ketus*, bear up that Jātavedas, the Sun, for the sight of all beings. Whom else, other than Āditya, would one call god?"
mine and tentative: "You rise facing all this; 'facing' is said of this light; you look upon all this facing it."

mine and tentative, doubtful: "*Bhuraṇyu* is a name for 'swift'. The *bhuraṇyu* is a bird: it carries over a long road; or the carrier of the world of heaven, he who flies together with it, is *bhuraṇyu*, by this [verse] called *pāvaka*. 'You, Varuṇa, look upon the nourishing (world) in order': 'that of you we praise' is the remainder of the sentence."
mine and tentative: "You go through the heaven and the wide, great expanse, the world, and the days, measuring them out with the nights, seeing the born beings, O Sūrya."
mine and tentative: "this Saura mantra, *udyann adya*, destroys sin, destroys disease and poison, and gives the fruit of enjoyment and of liberation."
mine and tentative: "*adri* may be from *ā-dṛ* 'to split' (one splits with it), or from *ad* 'to eat'; 'they are soma-eaters', so it is known."

mine and tentative, and incomplete where the print is doubtful: "Indra opened the cave of Vala; the best animal that was there, seizing it by the back, he dug out [*udakkhidat*]; a thousand animals followed it up; it became raised (*unnata*). He who desires cattle should offer this Indra-victim, the raised one; he runs to Indra with his own share; he gives him cattle; he becomes possessed of cattle, he becomes raised."
mine and tentative: "this sacrificial post is the thunderbolt; it is to be made eight-cornered, for the thunderbolt is eight-cornered."

mine and tentative, rough: "Indra, having killed Vṛtra and routed the Asuras, did not get hold of the Asura Namuci; [Śacī] seized him; the two grappled; he became the stronger of the two. He said: 'Let us make a compact; then I shall release you: do not kill me with dry or with wet, neither by day nor by night.' He [Indra] sprinkled this foam of the waters. It was neither dry nor wet, the dawn had come but the sun had not risen; this was neither day nor night. With the foam of the waters he cut off his head; [the head] followed him, [crying] 'Mitra-traitor!' He produced these *apāmārga* plants, offered them; by them he drove away the Rākṣasas; therefore there is an *apāmārga*-oblation, for the removal of the Rākṣasas."
mine and tentative: "when, at the slaying of Parṇaya or the slaying of Karañja, in the great Vṛtra-battle, I was heard forth."

mine and tentative: "*vṛndin* is from *vṛnd* [a root] of the action of becoming soft; 'when you pour down on the head of the sounding wind and of the drying sun, roaring, the *vana*, or [= the *dhana*]' — [the Nirukta] says 'the waters' or 'the riches' (?)"
mine and tentative, incomplete: "…therefore you are named 'sounding ones' (*nadyaḥ*); those are your names, rivers."
mine and tentative: "This best of lights has come, the bright, wide-shining sign has been born; as one impelled by Savitṛ for his urging, so Night has yielded her womb to Uṣas."

mine and tentative: "making both parents great, Agni was born, heaven and earth, with abundant seed." — "It says that heaven and earth are Agni's mother and father: for the sake of the great Agni's abiding the earth and atmosphere became very wide."
mine and tentative: "the friend [or: gift] of the Bhṛgus, the Uśij, of poet's wisdom."
my gloss, tentative: 'as [a seer like] Nodhas makes his dear things manifest'
